stem: A hospice patient needs a Schedule II narcotic. The prescriber faxes a valid prescription to the pharmacy and clearly indicates on the prescription that the patient is a hospice patient. What is the federal consequence of those facts?

choices.text: The fax may serve as the original Schedule II prescription under the hospice narcotic exception.
The fax is an original only if the patient also resides in an LTCF.
Hospice status permits refills on the Schedule II prescription.
The pharmacy must wait for a paper original before dispensing in every hospice case.
The notation is irrelevant because hospice exceptions apply only to Schedule III-V drugs.

explanation.core_reasoning: A properly designated hospice Schedule II narcotic prescription may use the fax as the original under federal law.

choice_analysis.A: The required hospice facts activate the exception.
choice_analysis.C: The fax exception does not create C-II refills.
choice_analysis.D: That would erase the federal exception.
choice_analysis.E: The exception specifically addresses C-II narcotics.

related_facts: Hospice notation is material to this exception.
explanation.mpje_trap: Confusing a fax exception with refill authorization.

reasoning_steps: Classify the drug as a Schedule II narcotic
